cases.complaint_text: I attended a real estate and investment networking event in Dubai where I met a representative of an international investment consultancy specialising in citizenship by investment. After several meetings I paid a processing fee of AED 25,000 and later a second milestone payment of AED 250,000 to the account they provided (Mubarak Salem, 5660609, AE600340005660609). After the second payment the representative gave excuses about government delays and then stopped responding.

report.typology: Advance-fee investment fraud through a front consultancy
report.narrative: Mysmo Gamal met a man calling himself Karim at a real-estate networking event in Dubai in May 2026. Karim presented Global Pathways Investment Consultancy as an international firm handling citizenship-by-investment applications and provided a company profile, brochure and registration documents. After several meetings Mr Gamal agreed to proceed. On 10 June he paid a 'citizenship application processing fee' of AED 25,000 to Mubarak Salem, account 5660609, IBAN AE600340005660609. He then received emails and documents stating that due diligence was complete and initial security approval granted. On 14 July, on the strength of those documents, he paid a second milestone of AED 250,000 to the same account (reference TRX-2026-10482). Communication then deteriorated into explanations about government processing delays and additional verification. By 29 July the representative had stopped responding and no application could be verified with any authority. Mr Gamal reported the matter at the station on 5 August.

evidence_assessment.finding: Stock imagery; license number belongs to a cancelled management-consultancy license
Sent from a free webmail domain, not the company domain
Both reconcile with the complainant's bank statement
Template document; issuing authority denies issuance

report.investigation_summary: The consultancy was never licensed for immigration services and its license was cancelled in April 2026; the account holder is the license signatory. Bank disclosure shows AED 180,000 cash-out and AED 60,000 to a virtual-asset exchange within 72 hours. KYC address and mobile are shared with the holder of account 3456660 (FC-2026-0204).

cases.complaint_text: I bought a gaming PC and console bundle from a seller called TechDeals UAE on a classifieds site. The seller (+971 55 302 8817) asked for a bank transfer to Abdullah Mohammed, account 3456660, IBAN AE750340003456660. I paid AED 8,900 on 20 August. Nothing was delivered and the listing and profile were deleted.

report.typology: Disposable classifieds storefront with personal collection account
report.narrative: Rashid Khalfan found a discounted gaming PC and console bundle listed by 'TechDeals UAE' on a classifieds platform on 18 August 2026. He contacted the seller on WhatsApp (+971 55 302 8817), who confirmed availability and requested a bank transfer to a personal account — Abdullah Mohammed, account 3456660, IBAN AE750340003456660 — with delivery promised within two days. Mr Khalfan transferred AED 8,900 on 20 August and sent the confirmation. The seller acknowledged the payment, then stopped replying the following day. The listing and the seller profile were deleted on 22 August. Mr Khalfan filed this report through the e-Crime portal on 28 August with the listing screenshots, the chat, the transfer confirmation and his bank statement.

evidence_assessment.finding: Reconciles with bank statement entry of 20 Aug

report.investigation_summary: Funds were withdrawn at ATMs the same evening. The seller phone is a prepaid SIM under an unverified identity. Bank KYC for account 3456660 shares an address and mobile with the holder of account 5660609 (FC-2026-0187).

cases.complaint_text: I received an SMS saying my card would be blocked and clicked the link, which asked for my banking login and an OTP. Within twenty minutes five transfers totalling AED 43,200 left my account to accounts I do not know. My bank has blocked the card and asked me to file a report.

I found a two-bedroom apartment in Al Barsha on a property site at a very good price. The agent sent a tenancy contract and asked for a deposit of AED 18,000 to secure it. After paying he stopped answering and the building security told me the apartment is occupied and not for rent.

report.typology: Deposit fraud via cloned property listing
report.narrative: Omar Saeed responded to a listing for a two-bedroom apartment in Al Barsha on 9 September 2026. The 'agent' communicated only on WhatsApp, sent a tenancy contract bearing a real brokerage's name, and pressed for a deposit of AED 18,000 to secure the unit before a viewing. Mr Saeed transferred the deposit on 12 September to a personal account. The agent then stopped responding, and building security confirmed the apartment is occupied. Mr Saeed filed this report on 15 September.

cases.complaint_text: I joined a Telegram trading group and was guided to deposit into a trading platform that showed profits. I deposited AED 96,000 over five weeks through a crypto exchange. When I tried to withdraw they asked for a 20% tax payment first and then blocked my account.

report.narrative: Khalid Al Mazrouei was added to a Telegram trading group in July 2026 where a 'mentor' posted daily signals. He was guided to register on a trading platform, converted funds through a licensed crypto exchange and deposited the equivalent of AED 96,000 in five transfers between 22 July and 28 August. The platform displayed growing profits. When he requested a withdrawal on 3 September, he was told to pay a 20% 'tax' first; on refusal, his account was blocked and the group administrators removed him. He reported the matter on 11 September with 22 Telegram screenshots, platform screenshots and his exchange history.

report.investigation_summary: The platform domain is 6 weeks old and the two receiving wallets consolidate to a single address flagged in two other jurisdictions' warnings. Exchange disclosure requested 12 September.

cases.complaint_text: Our accounts department received an email from what appeared to be our regular supplier notifying a change of bank account. Two invoice payments totalling AED 310,000 were made to the new account before the genuine supplier queried non-payment.

report.narrative: Meridian Trading LLC received an email on 19 August 2026 from an address differing from its supplier's genuine domain by one character, notifying a change of bank account for future invoices. The accounts department updated the beneficiary record and paid two genuine invoices, AED 185,000 on 24 August and AED 125,000 on 28 August, to the new account. The supplier queried non-payment on 1 September. The company's bank initiated a recall and the company filed this report on 2 September.

cases.complaint_text: I met someone on a dating application who said he was an engineer working abroad. Over three months he asked for help with medical bills and a customs problem and I sent six transfers totalling AED 54,500. He then disappeared.

report.typology: Long-con relationship fraud with emergency pretexts
report.narrative: The complainant met a man on a dating application in May 2026 who described himself as an engineer on an overseas contract. Over three months he built a relationship by daily messaging and video calls he always cut short. From June he requested help with medical bills, then a customs problem with a shipment of gifts. The complainant made six transfers totalling AED 54,500 between 12 June and 15 August to three different personal accounts. After the last payment all contact stopped. The report was filed on 24 August with a 140-page chat export and the six transfer confirmations.
